## Before you start

- **Designed for:** learners with little or no programming experience.
- **You are ready when:** you can use a web browser and are willing to predict,
  run, explain, and change small examples. No mathematics prerequisite is
  assumed.
- **Practice setup:** start with generated Colab notebooks. Unit 1 explains
  local workflows before later project units use environments and command-line
  tools.

::: {.callout-note title="Required does not mean install everything immediately"}
Local Python Tools is required because every learner should understand the
workflow and choose a practice environment deliberately. You can complete its
browser-based comparisons before installing local software, then return to the
setup steps when project-focused units begin.
:::

## What you will be able to do

- trace values through decisions, loops, collections, and functions;
- choose data structures and function boundaries that make behavior explainable;
- read tracebacks, reduce failures, validate input, and work safely with files;
- organize a repeatable project with dependencies, a CLI, tests, typing, and CI;
- use classes, iteration patterns, decorators, context managers, logging, and
  configuration when they improve the design;
- build and defend a complete Python project using tests, output, explanations,
  and debugging evidence.

## Required learning sequence

Python Foundations curriculum version 3 has **20 focused instructional units**,
five milestone checkpoints, and **Unit 21**, the final project. Units stay small
enough to name one coherent subject; milestone checkpoints ask you to integrate
several neighboring units.

### Milestone 1: Core Programming

| Unit | Focus |
|---|---|
| 1. [Getting Started](units/getting-started/index.qmd) | Choose a practice environment and run Python work reproducibly. |
| 2. [Values, Types, and Input/Output](units/values-types-input-output/index.qmd) | Represent information with Python values and exchange text with a learner. |
| 3. [Control Flow](units/control-flow/index.qmd) | Choose which instructions run, repeat work, and trace changing state. |

[Open Milestone 1: Core Programming](milestones/core-programming.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Milestone 2: Data and Functions

| Unit | Focus |
|---|---|
| 4. [Data Structures](units/data-structures/index.qmd) | Choose containers that match the relationships in your data. |
| 5. [Functions](units/functions/index.qmd) | Give reusable behavior a clear input, result, contract, and check. |

[Open Milestone 2: Data and Functions](milestones/data-and-functions.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Milestone 3: Debugging and Data Boundaries

| Unit | Focus |
|---|---|
| 6. [Debugging](units/debugging/index.qmd) | Investigate failures from evidence instead of changing code by guesswork. |
| 7. [Files and Structured Data](units/files/index.qmd) | Move data safely between a Python program and external files. |
| 8. [Error Handling and Validation](units/error-handling-and-validation/index.qmd) | Reject invalid input clearly and handle only failures the program understands. |

[Open Milestone 3: Debugging and Data Boundaries](milestones/debugging-and-data-boundaries.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Milestone 4: Reliable Python Projects

| Unit | Focus |
|---|---|
| 9. [Modules and Packages](units/modules-and-packages/index.qmd) | Split reusable Python code across importable files and package namespaces. |
| 10. [Project Structure](units/project-structure/index.qmd) | Arrange source, tests, configuration, and documentation predictably. |
| 11. [Environments and Dependencies](units/environments-and-dependencies/index.qmd) | Make a project runtime isolated and reproducible. |
| 12. [Command-Line Programs](units/command-line-programs/index.qmd) | Turn a reusable program into a command with explicit arguments and output. |
| 13. [Testing](units/testing/index.qmd) | Protect observable behavior with focused automated tests. |
| 14. [Code Style and Linting](units/code-style-and-linting/index.qmd) | Use automated tools to make code consistent and reveal likely mistakes. |
| 15. [Typing](units/typing/index.qmd) | Document value expectations and check them before runtime. |
| 16. [Automation and CI](units/automation-and-ci/index.qmd) | Run the project quality agreement automatically before and after sharing changes. |

[Open Milestone 4: Reliable Python Projects](milestones/reliable-projects.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Milestone 5: Abstractions and Application Patterns

| Unit | Focus |
|---|---|
| 17. [Object-Oriented Programming](units/object-oriented-programming/index.qmd) | Model cohesive state and behavior without hiding unnecessary complexity. |
| 18. [Comprehensions and Iteration](units/comprehensions-and-iteration/index.qmd) | Express transformations clearly and produce sequences eagerly or lazily. |
| 19. [Decorators and Context Managers](units/decorators-and-context-managers/index.qmd) | Apply reusable behavior around functions and resource lifecycles. |
| 20. [Logging and Configuration](units/logging-and-configuration/index.qmd) | Separate operational evidence and settings from core program behavior. |

[Open Milestone 5: Abstractions and Application Patterns](milestones/abstractions-and-application-patterns.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Unit 21: [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd)

Integrate the complete course in one small, explainable, tested project.

## Completion requirements and assessment

Python Foundations curriculum version 3 is locally complete when you have:

1. completed all **38 required lessons**;
2. recorded all **five required milestone checkpoints** after meeting their
   knowledge and practical thresholds;
3. built the required [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd) and
   self-assessed every rubric row as **Meets the requirement**.

Lesson quizzes remain formative and do not have a stored grade. There are no
optional lessons in this course.

::: {.callout-important title="Local completion is not a verified certificate"}
The completion dashboard is a private, self-reported browser record. It does not
verify identity, submit checkpoint artifacts, grade the project, or issue a
certificate. A verifiable certificate remains planned as a separate service.
:::

## Practice and next step

Treat each lesson as a lab: predict, run, explain, modify, and keep evidence.
Each milestone checkpoint combines several focused concepts, and the final
project connects all 20 instructional units.
